stem: Karim has noted the lifespans, in weeks, of a large random sample of certain insects. He carries out a test, at the 1% significance level, for the population mean, $\mu$. Karim’s null hypothesis is $\mu = 6.4$.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Given that Karim’s test is two-tail, state the alternative hypothesis.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: Karim finds that the value of the test statistic is $z = 2.43$.
parts.text: Explain what conclusion he should draw.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Explain briefly when a one-tail test is appropriate, rather than a two-tail test.
